documents.unit: Center for the Advancement of Teaching and Learning (CATL), Office of Education
documents.title: MUSC AI Acceptable Use Framework for Academic Tasks
documents.stance_why: The page introduces a five-category framework in which 'instructors will specify one of five categories of AI use for each task' (No AI, AI Planning, AI Limited, AI Extensive, AI Exploration). It sets no single default and says 'This is not a policy statement', so it offers tiers and hands the decision to instructors: delegates.
documents.summary: CATL's page presents MUSC's AI Acceptable Use Framework for Academic Tasks, a five-level scale instructors assign per task, with optional documentation at each level. It also describes support tools for faculty (syllabus language, icons, an assessment redesign bot) and links to the Honor Council integrity process. The framework is described as guidance, not a policy statement.

notes: Single included document. Page is mostly framework description with embedded video transcripts (framework video and Honor Code orientation video); anchors from transcripts are limited to single caption lines. The detailed framework document and the Plagiarism and AI Guideline were not accessible. Honor Code units are not AI-specific and were coded sparingly. No computing unit or course documents exist.
